solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who's given up religion, a humourless condition

parts.note: PO is short for po-faced, meaning humourless and disapproving
a condition or state of affairs

explanation.surface: A dry definition of someone who has lost their faith, as if being godless meant being joyless.
explanation.walkthrough: PO for humourless comes from 'po-faced', a British word for prim and solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is a person who has renounced their former religious faith.

clue.text: One has wide knowledge being amply hot quizzically

indicators.note: done in a puzzling, odd way, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A learned person is described, oddly, as being amply hot in a quizzical way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quizzically' rearranges AMPLY HOT; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person whose knowledge spans many different subjects.

clue.text: Bold swordsman won in band fastening on King

indicators.note: the letter for won sits inside the word for band

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist
W is the abbreviation for won in sports results
a buckle is a fastening on a belt or strap
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A medal-winning fencer is described by the sash and buckle of his costume and his royal connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A swashbuckler is a daring, flamboyant adventurer, classically a swordsman of the stage or screen.

clue.text: Charge a Tory leader with sleaze

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the opening of Tory

parts.note: tack is cheap, tasteless or shoddy stuff, the root of tacky

explanation.surface: A political jab: accuse a Conservative party leader of sleaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to rush forward and attack, as cavalry or a bull does.

clue.text: Blade used for apple peeling

indicators.note: the letters of apple peeling are used to supply the answer, which runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip on which knife to use for peeling an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a fencing sword, so a blade in the swordsman's sense.

clue.text: A certain type restraining tense hanger-on

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it, as if keeping it in check

parts.note: Courier is a typeface, so one particular type in the printer's sense
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone of a certain sort keeps a nervous hanger-on in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' is printing type: Courier is the typewriter-style font, not a kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends a royal court, and the word is used for a sycophantic follower of the powerful.

clue.text: Weedy type with one person at Westminster

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP, a Member of Parliament, sits at Westminster in London

explanation.surface: A jibe at a feeble politician who has joined a member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person, which is what weedy describes in British slang.

clue.text: Reptile injured a printer

indicators.note: damaged or hurt, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A news item about a printer hurt by a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which is a reptile.

clue.text: Instruction to turn over state compound possibly harmful

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, printed at the foot of a page
Maine is a state of the USA

explanation.surface: A warning note on a leaflet about a chemical that may be dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are compounds formed in rotting protein, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Football bosses hold the French jumper

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, governs English football
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: English football's governing body keeps hold of a French player, a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is not a sweater (British for a pullover) but something that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is an insect famous for jumping huge distances relative to its size.

clue.text: Landworker's allotment failure

definitions.note: read as landworker is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: an allotment is a portion or share
to come a cropper is to fail badly

explanation.surface: A farmhand's vegetable allotment has done poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment' suggests a British rented vegetable plot, but here it is just a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharecropper farms rented land and pays the landlord with part of the crop.

clue.text: Crowd free news item

parts.note: to press is to crowd in on someone
to release is to set free

explanation.surface: A mob is set free, as reported in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A press release is a statement issued to journalists for publication as news.

clue.text: Fleece essayist's relatives

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia, so the essayist's is Lamb's
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A writer's family is fleeced.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb was an early 19th-century English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: A lambskin is the skin of a lamb with the wool on, a fleece.

clue.text: Nick's word denying church

definitions.note: read as nick is, the 's linking definition and wordplay

parts.note: not is the word used to deny or negate

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick says no to churchgoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick.

clue.text: Step back after one cold Arctic feature

indicators.note: the turned word comes after the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: the word for step is read from the end to the start

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: Instructions to step back after feeling cold, like an Arctic explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice covering polar land, as at the Arctic.

clue.text: Babe mostly in fashion

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman, as babe is

explanation.surface: A good-looking young woman who mostly follows fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, which is to say fashionable.

clue.text: Applauded chat heard as nonsense

indicators.note: a word as spoken stands for how it is spelt in the grid

parts.note: clapped, which said aloud is the same as clapt
rap is slang for talk or chat

explanation.surface: Hearing applauded chatter dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns CLAPPED into the sound-alike CLAPT; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious or insincere talk, nonsense meant to win applause.

clue.text: Provide food consumed in Costa Rica

indicators.note: the word for consumed goes inside the country's letters

parts.note: CR is the international code for Costa Rica
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Feeding people with food eaten in Costa Rica.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food and drink, as for an event.

clue.text: Noisily drink litre for amusement

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and make merry noisily

explanation.surface: Downing a litre of drink loudly, just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amusement' is a fairground amusement, a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, a fairground amusement ride.

clue.text: Turned to bridge

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of spin, as in spun
to cross from one side to the other, to stretch across

explanation.definitionFit: Span is an archaic past tense of spin, and to span a gap is to bridge it.

clue.text: Word puzzle like clues above mostly getting habitual response

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped, keeping most of it

parts.note: the clues above these in the puzzle are the across ones
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue: a puzzle described in terms of its across clues and a nervous habit.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which initial letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: Ensnaring line, annoy fisherman

indicators.note: one word traps the other inside it

parts.note: to anger is to annoy

explanation.surface: A fisherman's tangled line annoys him.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is someone who fishes with a rod and line.

clue.text: Crowd see round end of bar in pub

parts.note: a host is a large crowd

indicators.note: the cathedral city's name goes round the letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city whose bishop has a see, a diocese

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of bar

explanation.surface: Drinkers watch a crowd gather round the bar in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; crosswords use ELY because Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned word for an inn or pub.

clue.text: Onset of illness following rogue food

indicators.note: the picked letter follows the word for rogue

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal or rogue

indicators.note: the onset is the start, the first letter of illness

explanation.surface: Feeling ill after eating dodgy food.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAMPI are breaded langoustines, a British pub staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi is a dish of fried breaded langoustine tails, a food.

clue.text: Cooked hot unsophisticated food in this way

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or messed about

parts.note: rough means crude or unsophisticated
fare is food

explanation.surface: A recipe: rustic food cooked hot in this style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges HOT to THO; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or public way through a place.

clue.text: Gershwin hero failing to start revel

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Porgy is the hero of Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: An opera hero fails to get his party started.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild revel or drunken party.

clue.text: Can't stand sticky heat

indicators.note: sticky suggests something awkward or messy, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A complaint about humid, sticky weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to be unable to stand it.

clue.text: A voice regularly expressed in ballot-box

indicators.note: every other letter of ballot-box is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A voter's voice is expressed regularly through the ballot-box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' suggests a say in an election; it is a singing voice. 'expressed in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a vocal range, a lower female or high male singing voice.

clue.text: Stick in an opening exchange of views

indicators.note: the word for stick goes inside the other two

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Poking a stick into a gap to start a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a heated exchange of differing views.

clue.text: Distinction shown by modern artist from 'ere

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a modern British artist
the dropped h of 'ere says hence loses its h, giving 'ence

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding remark about a distinguished artist from around here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' means hence; 'ere, with its h dropped as in Cockney speech, shows that hence loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is distinction or fame, high standing in a field.
